output.title: Design out the error that feeds itself
output.body:
When a workflow keeps correcting its own mistakes, the real problem is often not the last error. It is the loop that sends bad data back into the same process.

A bounded question I would ask is: which repeated manual task creates the next round of rework? If you enter invoice details by hand and then reconcile them by hand because the first pass was incomplete or misclassified, the workflow is teaching itself to repeat the same mistake. That is the loop to design against.

The next step is to check whether AI fits that workflow at all. Is it repetitive, does it produce a measurable outcome, and does it already live in digital documents or SaaS tools? If not, the cleaner move is to change the process, not add software.

If it does fit, define one error-blocking control before anything else. Duplicate detection, mandatory field validation, or human approval before a high-risk step all work as the same idea: catch the mistake before it can cycle back.

For a pilot, keep it to one workflow and one control. Not the whole business. That is usually enough to see whether the loop is actually broken, or just better dressed.
